thread.title: Tesla Bear Sees Shares Crashing 72% By 2019 | Investopedia

author: Shoshanna Delventhal
title: Tesla Bear Sees Shares Crashing 72% By 2019 | Investopedia
text:
Tesla Bear Sees Shares Crashing 72% By 2019 By Shoshanna Delventhal | April 12, 2018 — 11:31 AM EDT 
The polarizing debate on the Street over the future of Tesla Inc. ( TSLA ) just got a lot more interesting as one bear made a bold call for the stock to plummet to $84 by 2019. 
Vertical Research’s newly hired analyst Gordon Johnson, an infamous bear on solar-energy stocks, spoke to CNBC in an interview Wednesday highlighting new competition in the electric vehicle (EV) space as a huge threat to the market pioneer. While noting that "time and time again they have targeted production numbers that they haven't hit," Johnson stated that "the real issue with Tesla is competition." (See also: Tesla Overtakes Apple as Most-Shorted US Stock. ) 
Boutique research firm Vertical Group started Tesla at a sell rating last week, expecting shares to plummet a whopping 72% from a price just above $300 per share at Wednesday close. TSLA, which regained its position as the most shorted U.S. equity ahead of Apple Inc. ( AAPL ), according to a recent report by S3 Partners, has fallen 3.4% year-to-date (YTD) , underperforming the S&P 500 's 1.2% loss over the same period. Shares have sank 16% from their 2018 peak reached in February and have lost nearly a quarter of their value since all-time highs secured in 2017. Bear Sees Competition, Production Shortfalls Vexing EV Pioneer 
Johnson noted that last year, General Motor Co.'s ( GM ) Chevy Bolt became the "first non-Tesla, 100 percent battery electric car capable of 200 miles" to hit the market. As four more electric vehicles are slated for release in 2018, and 101 more through 2020, the analyst doubts that Elon Musk's EV pioneer can ramp up sales as it struggles to boost production of its first mass-market vehicle, the Model 3 sedan. 
The Vertical Research bear criticized Musk's series of broken promises, noting that in 2014, the CEO said the firm would product 60,000 Model X luxury vehicles in 2015, yet only produced 208. He added that Tesla expected to manufacture 1,600 Model 3s in the third quarter of 2017, ultimately falling far from the target at just about 200. 
While Musk eased investor worries regarding a potential capital raise in 2018, Johnson is not so convinced. He expects the firm to raise money in the coming year in order to increase production numbers. 
The note comes as on Wednesday, Reuters reported that Tesla is planning to roll out a sport utility vehicle called the Model Y by November 2019, with production in China beginning in 2021. (See also: China’s Stance on Tariffs Would Boost Tesla Most. )
